issues.legal_issue: A co-owner who is entitled to a share in a house may obtain partition and separate possession of that share when the family has separated in status but the house has not been divided by metes and bounds.
material_facts: The brothers had separated in status.
The house had not been divided by metes and bounds.
The respondents were entitled to a one-third share in the house.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were entitled to partition and separate possession of their one-third share in the house; the decree was modified to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Separation in status does not itself divide the house by metes and bounds. Where a claimant is entitled to a share and the house remains undivided, the claimant may seek partition and separate possession of that share. No earlier cases or statutory provisions were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: appeal_from_partition_decree and family_separated_in_status and house_not_divided_by_met es_and_bounds and claimant_entitled_to_a_share

predicates.appeal_from_partition_decree: The matter is an appeal from a decree in a suit seeking partition.
predicates.family_separated_in_status: The family members had separated in status.
predicates.house_not_divided_by_met es_and_bounds: The house had not been physically divided into separate portions by metes and bounds.
predicates.claimant_entitled_to_a_share: The claimant was entitled to a share in the house.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal concerns a house that remains physically undivided after the family has separated in status, a claimant entitled to a share may obtain partition and separate possession of that share.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not determine entitlement by succession to a widow’s share without adequately considering the disputed issue, particularly where the pleadings and issues do not address that basis of entitlement.
material_facts: The respondents claimed that the family remained joint and that their entitlement arose by survivorship, but that claim was rejected.
The trial court nevertheless concluded that the respondents inherited part of the widow’s share after her death.
The appellants specifically challenged whether the respondents were entitled to succeed to the widow’s share.
The High Court had not satisfactorily considered that question, and no issue had been framed on who inherited the widow’s share.
issues.conclusion: The question whether the respondents were entitled to succeed to the widow’s share was remitted to the High Court for consideration.
issues.legal_principle: A disputed basis of succession should not be resolved without adequate consideration of the issue and the parties’ pleadings. The trial court had relied on the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937, and the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, in describing the widow’s interest and its devolution; the Supreme Court did not decide the respondents’ entitlement under those provisions and remitted the question. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_partition_decree and widow_share_succession_disputed and succession_not_adequately_considered and (no_succession_issue_framed or succession_basis_not_pleaded)

predicates.appeal_from_partition_decree: The matter is an appeal from a decree in a suit seeking partition.
predicates.widow_share_succession_disputed: A party disputed whether the claimant inherited a deceased widow’s share.
predicates.succession_not_adequately_considered: The lower appellate court did not satisfactorily consider the disputed succession question.
predicates.no_succession_issue_framed: The trial court did not frame an issue identifying who inherited the widow’s share.
predicates.succession_basis_not_pleaded: The claimant’s pleadings did not set out succession as an alternative basis for entitlement.

issues.definition: In a partition appeal, when entitlement by succession to a widow’s share is disputed and has not been adequately considered, the succession question is remitted if it was not framed as an issue or pleaded as a basis of entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of a widow’s share cannot be upheld on the asserted basis of legal necessity when the purchaser fails to prove that necessity.
material_facts: The widow executed a sale of her share in the house to the appellants.
The trial court found that the appellants had not proved that the sale was for legal necessity.
The High Court affirmed that finding, and the Supreme Court agreed with the concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the sale was not supported by legal necessity was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The purchaser relying on a sale made by a widow had to establish that it was supported by legal necessity; the concurrent finding that this had not been proved was accepted. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_partition_decree: The matter is an appeal from a decree in a suit seeking partition.
predicates.widow_sold_share: A widow transferred her share in the property by sale.
predicates.purchaser_failed_to_prove_legal_necessit: The purchaser did not prove that the sale was made for legal necessity.

issues.definition: When a widow sells her share and the purchaser fails to prove legal necessity, the sale is not supported by legal necessity.
